SMTO-HTTP-0004 — SMTO couldn't reach the service's sign-in address

GUID: eb08b6cd-96ec-4b2e-84e4-1293477aa403
Slug: http-auth-transport-error
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • While signing in to the service before your request, the network connection to its sign-in address failed. Your main request wasn't sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the Gateway computer the connection uses is online and can open the service's website. SMTO signs in from the Gateway computer, so that computer needs a working path to the service.
  2. Open Parameter Store, select this HTTP Connection, and check Base URL and Login path or Token endpoint. A mistyped address sends the sign-in to a place that doesn't answer properly.
  3. If your network requires a proxy, check the Proxy settings under Advanced connection settings. A missing or wrong proxy stops the connection before it reaches the service.
  4. Select Test connection. The test signs in again and shows whether the connection now works.

What success looks like

  • Test connection reports Reachable and Authenticated.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your network or this HTTP Connection. If an earlier request that changes something was interrupted, check on the service whether it already went through before repeating it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Requests raised a non-TLS, non-timeout transport exception (for example connection refused or reset, name resolution or proxy failure) during the HTTP authentication exchange, before the resource request.

What this means

  • Requests raised a non-TLS, non-timeout transport exception during an authentication exchange. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Requests raised a non-TLS, non-timeout transport exception during an authentication exchange.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the authentication endpoint's execution evidence and Gateway network path without exposing credential values.

How to fix it

  • From the Gateway host, test the login or token endpoint resolved from the profile's Base URL (DNS, connectivity, and the profile's proxy settings under Advanced connection settings). Fix the route, endpoint or proxy, then rerun Test connection. If an earlier write in the same run was interrupted, verify its outcome on the service before repeating it.
  • Check the route and login endpoint transport. Inspect authentication effects before another attempt.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The login transport completes and the intended session is confirmed before resource work proceeds.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
